stories.title: The Contractor Who Took The Money
stories.hook: A contractor took my twenty-thousand-dollar deposit for a kitchen remodel and ghosted me, thinking an old widower wouldn't fight back.
stories.narration:
A contractor took my twenty-thousand-dollar deposit for a kitchen remodel and ghosted me, thinking an old widower wouldn't fight back. After my wife passed, I finally decided to update the kitchen the way she always wanted. I hired a local contractor named Marcus. He drove a flashy truck, had a smooth pitch, and insisted on a fifty percent deposit upfront for materials. Like a fool, I wrote him a check for twenty thousand dollars. 

For the first two weeks, he had an excuse every day. The cabinets were delayed. His crew was sick. His truck broke down. By week three, his phone was disconnected. I drove to the address on his business card and found an empty strip mall office. He had vanished with my money. Most people my age would have swallowed the loss and felt ashamed. But I spent forty years as a claims investigator for a major insurance firm. I hunt people for a living. 

I started digging. I pulled public records and found Marcus had filed for bankruptcy twice and operated under three different LLCs to avoid liability. I traced his flashy truck’s license plate through a private investigator friend and found his actual residence—a luxury apartment downtown. I also found out he was actively bidding on a massive, million-dollar commercial renovation project for a local restaurant chain. 

I didn't call the police; civil disputes over deposits take years and usually result in nothing. Instead, I compiled a comprehensive dossier of his bankruptcies, his shell companies, and the police reports from four other seniors he had defrauded. I printed five copies. I drove to the restaurant chain's corporate headquarters and requested a meeting with their procurement director. I laid the dossier on his desk. 

Marcus lost the million-dollar bid that afternoon. But I wasn't finished. I attended every home and garden trade show in the tri-state area where Marcus was exhibiting. I simply stood next to his booth in a tailored suit, handing out copies of his fraud records to every single person who approached him. 

On the third day, he approached me in the parking lot, sweating profusely. He handed me a cashier's check for twenty-five thousand dollars—my deposit, plus five thousand for my 'trouble'—and begged me to stop. I took the check, cashed it, and immediately forwarded his dossier to the state licensing board anyway. 

His contractor's license was permanently revoked the following month. My new kitchen looks beautiful.
stories.description: He stole my deposit and vanished. He didn't know I spent forty years hunting people for a living.
